questions.question: Explain the long-term and immediate causes of the Soweto uprising.
questions.expected_answer: Long-term: Bantu Education Act 1953 (Verwoerd); spending on white pupil more than ten times that on black pupil; overcrowding (60+ per class), double sessions, under-qualified teachers, few books, fees; township conditions in Soweto (about a million people, crowded houses, no electricity, pass laws, no say); economic slowdown, unemployment, rising prices; 1973 Durban strikes; expanded secondary schooling and double intake in 1976. Immediate: 1974 Afrikaans Medium Decree, half the subjects in Afrikaans from Standard 5 (Treurnicht, M.C. Botha); teachers and pupils struggled; Afrikaans seen as language of the oppressor; objections ignored; boycotts from early 1976 (Orlando West Junior Secondary).

questions.question: Explain the role of Black Consciousness and the student leaders.
questions.expected_answer: Black Consciousness: Steve Biko, SASO (1968/69), BPC (1972); psychological liberation, pride, self-reliance, black-led struggle, "black" included Africans, coloured people, Indians. Spread via SASM and young teachers. 13 June 1976: SASM action committee (later SSRC), led by Tsietsi Mashinini (Morris Isaacson), Seth Mazibuko, Murphy Morobe; peaceful march to Orlando Stadium; plan kept secret; placards. Debate: planned networks plus student decisions.

questions.question: Describe the events of 16 June 1976.
questions.expected_answer: About 10 000-20 000 students marched in columns, singing; police confronted them near Orlando West High School; disputed start (stones, dog, tear gas); police fired live ammunition; Hastings Ndlovu (15) and Hector Pieterson (12) killed; Sam Nzima photograph of Mbuyisa Makhubo carrying Hector with Antoinette Sithole; anger: WRAB offices, beer halls, bottle stores burned; Dr Melville Edelstein killed; Kruger blamed agitators; Vorster: order at all costs; decree withdrawn 6 July 1976; 16 June now Youth Day.
